title: Music Cultures of the World: Indonesia
description: Introduces Indonesian musical and cultural practices through folk, classical, popular musics; religious traditions, theater and dance. Topics include interconnection of sonic and social structures, historical conditions of colonial and postcolonial relationships with the West, and transitions to contemporary transnational circulations.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division.

title: Music in Modern Japan
description: This course explores music and culture in modern Japan. What kind of society do we hear in its diverse mix of sounds and musical practices? We explore this question through traditional genres, national politics, and transnational exchanges of popular media.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division.

title: Music Cultures of the World: Other Regions
description: A study of music traditions and genres from other regions of the world. Specific regions studied vary by quarter and are announced in advance by the department.

title: Music Culture of the Polish Tatra Mountains
description: The Tatras are the home of a distinct folk culture, including music based on polyphonic singing ad violin ensembles. Course investigates the present-day music from this region and its history, and examines the influence of tourism and ethnography on the music-culture.

title: American Folk Music: Old-Time, Bluegrass and Country
description: Study of English-language American folk music, using mixed-media tools for learning. The focus is on string band music often associated with Appalachia and usually called "old-time," and the distinct but related styles of bluegrass and country.

title: Eco-Acoustic-Arts: Sounding & Creating with Global Environmental Elements
description: In eco-acoustic-arts, students investigate & create with geo and bio elements (including water, plants, rocks, animals). Using sounding as an inspirational process to explore ecological entanglements (scientific, cultural, artistic), methods include sensory ethnography, ethography, mapping & digital technologies.
prerequisites_raw: Upper division standing, instructor approval required.

title: Music, Community, Wellbeing: Advocacy and Activism
description: Taking a vocational and facilitatory approach, this course uses case studies to explore concepts and processes of generating and sustaining musical activity as community-engaged practice. Topics include: social justice, health and wellbeing, education, senses of place, ecology, and technology.
prerequisites_raw: Upper division standing, instructor approval.

title: Musics in Mexico
description: An exploration of a range of musics of Mexico, contextualized in their historical, political, ideological, and social milieu. Encompassing discussion, readings, and performance. (No prior instrumental skills required.)
prerequisites_raw: No prior instrumental skills required.

title: Studies in Ethnomusicology
description: An introduction to the field of ethnomusicology using theories and methods derived from the social sciences and humanities. Topic areas to include transcription and analysis, musicians, musical instruments, music acculturation, and the function of music in society.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing.

title: STDS RENAISS MUSIC
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 12A-B-C OR PERMISSION OF INSTRUCTOR. PRIMARILY FOR THE MAJOR EMPHASIZHISTORY AND THEORY.

title: Proseminar in Baroque Music
description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of Baroque music.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; Music 10-A-B-C.

title: Proseminar in Classical Music
description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of classical music.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; Music 10A-B-C.

title: Proseminar in Romantic Music
description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of romantic music.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; Music 10A-B-C.

title: Proseminar in Contemporary Music
description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of contemporary music.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; Music 10A-B-C.

title: Ethnomusicology Forum
description: A forum for the presentation of research and performance by students, faculty, and visiting scholars and performers.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor.

title: Special Topics
description: Special seminar in selected problems of current musicology, ethnomusicology, theory, or performance.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

title: B.A. Senior Project

title: Junior Composition Portfolio

prerequisites_raw: Passing of B.M. sophomore audition; and, consent of instructor; open to upper-division Bachelor of Music Composition Emphasis major only.

title: Honors Music
description: An undergraduate independent research for honor students. Carefully selected topics intended to foster excellence in research, theory, composition, or performance.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; honors students only; consent of instructor and department.

title: Senior Recital
description: Preparation of senior recital.

title: Senior Composition Portfolio and Recital
description: Preparation of senior composition portfolio.
prerequisites_raw: Passing of junior composition portfolio; and, consent of instructor; open tsenior BM Composition emphasis majors only.

title: Readings In Music
description: Critical review and discussion of related topics in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112A-F series; consent of instructor.

title: Individual Research in Music
description: Independent research under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Course offers qualified students the opportunity to undertake independent research or work in a research group in topics in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112AB-F series; consent of instructor.

title: Independent Research Assistance in Music
description: Faculty supervised research assistance.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112AB-F series; consent of instructor and department.

title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
description: A survey of music bibliography and research methods.

title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
description: Survey and discussion of select historical, methodological, and theoretical approaches to research in musicology.

title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
description: Survey of bibliographic sources and individual research projects in ethonomusicology.

title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
description: A survey of music bibliography and research methods in theory.

title: Notation and Music: Their Historical Interrelation
description: White mensural notation, lute and keyboard tablatures.

title: Seminar in Musicology
description: May be repeated for credit. Seminar in musicology. First quarter of a two-quarter doctoral seminar dealing with selected topics in musicology.
prerequisites_raw: M.A. or equivalent with consent of instructor. For advanced students only.

title: Seminar in Musicology.
description: Taken upon completion of Music 202A. Seminar in musicology. Second quarter of a two-quarter doctoral seminar dealing with selected topics in musicology.
prerequisites_raw: M.A. or equivalent with consent of instructor. For advanced students only. Music 202A.

title: Musicology-Theory Forum
description: Theory students, faculty and visiting scholars present their current research.
prerequisites_raw: Graduate standing in musicology or theory emphasis.
